claims.text: A coupled ab initio electron–phonon and machine-learned anharmonic lattice-dynamics framework will separately predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The separate lattice and electronic conductivity predictions will be accurate.
The new framework will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 25–30% relative to Debye-temperature-based and force-constant-variation models.
Explicitly capturing local atomic disorder will improve thermal-conductivity predictions for HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicitly capturing anharmonic effects will improve thermal-conductivity predictions for HfNbTaTiZr.
Accounting for scattering from approximately 1 wt.% oxygen will improve thermal-conductivity predictions.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can provide a useful representation of interactions in a multicomponent refractory alloy.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials can achieve accuracy near that of their underlying DFT calculations.
The proposed machine-learned potential can supply anharmonic lattice-dynamical corrections for HfNbTaTiZr.
Local disorder and anharmonic variations in interatomic force constants mediate phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Ab initio electron–phonon calculations combined with machine-learned lattice dynamics can decouple electronic and lattice heat-transport channels.
The lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are nearly equal below 200 K.
From 300 to 1200 K, the predicted lattice and electronic contributions will sum to a total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m).
A HfNbTaTiZr specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen has experimentally reported total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m) between 300 and 1200 K.
Existing DFT-elastic-property and simplified lattice-dynamics approaches do not decouple electronic and lattice heat-transport channels.
Existing simplified approaches do not capture oxygen-impurity effects in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed model's deviation from experiment will be 25–30% lower than that of earlier approaches.
Seebeck and frequency-resolved thermal-conductivity measurements can provide separate lattice and electronic conductivity values for the proposed comparison.
Predictions outside near-equilibrium conditions or beyond slight oxygen contamination may not retain the stated validity.
